items.title: ‘Fancy cars hold no appeal’: We have a 99% chance of outliving our life savings. Why not spend, spend, spend?
items.content: “I’m 68, she’s 74, and we’re both in good health. We married later in life and have no children.”

items.title: Inflation surges, PCE shows. Fed pause on rate hikes unlikely to last long with prices still rising.
items.content: Even though the Federal Reserve temporarily put its inflation fight on hold this week, the cost of living rose sharply again last month in a sign the central bank’s work is far from done.

items.title: U.S. economy grows at fastest pace in almost three years, third-quarter GDP shows
items.content: The U.S. economy ripped off its fastest rate of growth in almost three years, amped up by the boom in artificial intelligence and strong spending by wealthier Americans.

items.title: Caterpillar’s stock heads for worst day in 7 years — and what that means for the Dow
items.content: Caterpillar’s data center business is fine, but other areas disappointed and the stock was heading for its biggest loss in years.

items.title: Lilly raised sales guidance for third time this year as Zepbound sales soar. Its stock is rallying.
items.content: The drugmaker continues to dominate the market for prescription weight-loss drugs in the U.S.

items.title: It’s the strangest job market the U.S. has ever seen. The low-hire, low-fire economy turns 3 years old.
items.content: America has always been a job-creating machine. It has broken down for three straight years, and the implications could be with us for a long time.

items.title: Is it dumb to take travel advice from influencers?

items.title: You can’t rely on the S&P 500 as much as you may think
items.content: The index’s weakness may surprise a generation of investors raised on the cult of “stocks always go up.”

items.title: We’re in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage — or put the money in a high-yield savings account?
items.content: “Let’s say 10 years from now, when I’m 84, we need a substantial amount of cash.”

items.title: The Fed held off on a rate hike. Today’s GDP and inflation reports could make waiting harder.
items.content: GDP and inflation figures arrive together at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time. Strong growth and persistent price pressures could strengthen the case for an interest-rate increase in December.
